History:
- Main complaint: Shortness of breath with right-sided back pain on deep inspiration (pleuritic-type pain) starting today.
- Associated symptoms today: Subjective fever (not measured; assessed by touch), hemoptysis on two occasions, awareness of heart beating more than usual.
- Preceding symptoms: About 2 weeks of fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and greater difficulty with daily activities.
- No recent long-haul flights. Denies personal or family history of blood clots.
- Non-smoker. Works a desk job. Lives alone in a flat. Has a cat.
- No prior similar episodes documented.

Past Medical History:
- Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
- Medications: Methotrexate (dose/route/frequency not documented); last dose taken this morning.
- Allergies: No known drug or other allergies.
- No other chronic conditions reported. No hospitalizations mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Remote assessment via video:
  - Self-counted radial pulse: approximately 66–74 bpm (regular).
  - Capillary refill test via video: appeared normal/brisk.
  - Oropharyngeal inspection attempted via phone camera; findings not documented.
  - Cervical nodes self-palpated by patient: no enlargement felt.
  - Clinician impression: patient does not appear acutely unstable on video assessment.
- No vital signs (BP, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation) obtained.
- No chest auscultation performed (remote visit).

Impression:
- Acute shortness of breath with pleuritic right-sided back pain, hemoptysis, and subjective fever in a patient with SLE on methotrexate; concern for lower respiratory tract infection/pneumonia requiring in-person evaluation to rule out serious causes.

Management Plan:
- Arrange same-day, in-person clinic review for full assessment:
  - Chest auscultation, vital signs (BP, temperature, heart rate), and overall stability check.
- Antibiotics may be required pending in-person findings; no prescription issued during this remote visit.
- Consider chest X-ray if exam suggests pneumonia or if symptoms do not improve.
- Contact details provided in appointment notes to book the same-day face-to-face visit with a physician.
- Reassurance provided: presentation less suggestive of lung cancer given acute onset; further investigations may be considered based on exam and course.

Patient Summary:
- 45-year-old presenting with one day of dyspnea, pleuritic right-sided back pain, hemoptysis (twice), and subjective fever, following two weeks of fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance.
- Remote exam did not show acute instability; heart rate by self-check was normal range and capillary refill was brisk.
- Plan is urgent same-day in-person evaluation to examine the chest, obtain vitals, and initiate treatment as indicated; antibiotics likely if infection confirmed, with possible imaging if not improving.

Key Takeaways:
- Attend same-day in-person clinic visit for chest exam and vital signs; call the provided number to book.
- Antibiotics will be considered after examination; none prescribed yet.
- Lung cancer is considered unlikely based on the acute presentation, but follow-up (including possible chest X-ray) may be needed if symptoms persist.

Next Steps:
- Same-day face-to-face appointment for chest auscultation and full set of vitals.
- Initiate antibiotics if bacterial chest infection suspected on exam.
- Consider chest X-ray if examination warrants or if symptoms do not improve.
- Follow-up plan to be determined after in-person assessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - No documented vital signs: BP, temperature, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation.
  - No chest auscultation; no imaging or labs obtained.
  - Medication dose/route/frequency for methotrexate not documented; no full medication reconciliation.
  - No documentation of alcohol use, recent sick contacts, or vaccination status.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Patient provided two different names (“Tracy Chapman” initially and later “Doris”); conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Minor inaudible/noisy segments; some details (e.g., throat exam findings) not explicitly stated.
